figureLabel: My body – revisiting and describing
altText: KG2 learners revisiting a body features chart and describing parts of the body in more detail.
detailedDescription: The same classroom body-features illustration used in KG1, now used in KG2 to encourage learners to describe functions of each body part, compare similarities and differences, and talk about how to care for their bodies.

figureLabel: Personal hygiene and body parts – extension
altText: KG2 learners linking personal hygiene routines to specific body parts and their functions.
detailedDescription: Classroom scene of children practising hygiene such as washing hands and brushing teeth. In KG2 the teacher guides learners to explain why each action protects certain body parts and how neglect could affect health and daily activities.

figureLabel: Books and body parts – making deeper connections
altText: KG2 learners using a familiar book to relate pictures of body parts to how the body works and how we learn.
detailedDescription: A big book showing children and body parts is revisited in KG2. Learners not only name parts but also talk about how we use our eyes to read, our hands to hold books and our brains to understand, building stronger links between reading and real-life experience.

figureLabel: Body parts in action – skills and safety
altText: KG2 learners reflecting on activities that use different body parts and how to use them safely.
detailedDescription: The active play scene with jumping, hopping, walking on a line and threading beads is reused. In KG2, children talk about which body parts each activity uses, why balance and coordination matter, and how to avoid injury during such activities.

figureLabel: Daily hygiene routines – responsibility
altText: KG2 learners discussing how and why to take personal responsibility for daily hygiene routines.
detailedDescription: The hygiene corner image is reused. Instead of simply naming routines, KG2 learners discuss when and how often each routine should be done and how good hygiene affects friends, family and the community.

figureLabel: Family types and support systems
altText: KG2 learners comparing nuclear and extended families and discussing how family members support one another.
detailedDescription: The compound-house family scene is reused for KG2. Learners compare nuclear and extended family setups and talk about different ways families share responsibilities, care for children and support education.

figureLabel: Matching family duties – planning and fairness
altText: KG2 learners matching family duties to members and discussing fair sharing of work at home.
detailedDescription: The card-matching activity with family duties is reused. In KG2, pupils not only match duties but also discuss fairness, gender stereotypes, and how children can actively contribute in age-appropriate ways.

figureLabel: Family story – problem-solving in the home
altText: KG2 learners listening to a family story and suggesting how family members can solve simple problems together.
detailedDescription: The big-book family story is reused. In KG2, learners discuss challenges the family might face (e.g. busy parents, chores, homework) and suggest possible solutions, training early problem-solving and empathy.

figureLabel: Texts about families – comparing and contrasting
altText: KG2 learners interacting with texts about families and comparing them with their own home experiences.
detailedDescription: The family-texts image is reused for KG2 with a higher focus on comparing different family setups in books to real life, respecting differences and identifying positive values across examples.

figureLabel: Family love and respect – resolving conflicts
altText: KG2 learners discussing how love and respect help families solve problems peacefully.
detailedDescription: The warm family-compound scene is reused. In KG2, children role-play and discuss how to say sorry, forgive, and show respect when people disagree at home, preparing them for healthy future relationships.

figureLabel: Parts of the home – revisiting and comparing
altText: KG2 learners revisiting a picture of a home and naming and comparing different parts of the house.
detailedDescription: The same picture of a simple Ghanaian home used in KG1 is reused in KG2. Now learners identify parts of the home and talk about how each part is used, compare their homes with the picture, and discuss which spaces help them study, rest and play.

figureLabel: Home activities – roles and routines
altText: KG2 learners observing children role-playing home activities and discussing who does what at home.
detailedDescription: The dramatic play corner arranged like a home is reused. In KG2, learners describe different home activities, talk about who does each task in their own homes, and think about how children can share work fairly instead of leaving everything to adults or one person.

figureLabel: Stories about homes – similarities and differences
altText: KG2 learners listening to a story about a home and comparing it to their own home experiences.
detailedDescription: The home storybook scene is reused with deeper thinking. KG2 learners identify rooms and activities in the story, compare them with their own homes, and discuss what makes a home peaceful, safe and welcoming for everyone.

figureLabel: Home safety rules – preventing accidents
altText: KG2 learners looking at a home safety picture and suggesting how to prevent accidents in the home.
detailedDescription: The home safety scene is reused. KG2 learners identify possible dangers in and around the home, suggest safer choices, and talk about what to do if something goes wrong, training them to think ahead and protect themselves and others.

figureLabel: Physical features of the school – functions
altText: KG2 learners revisiting school buildings and spaces and explaining what each place is used for.
detailedDescription: The school compound picture is reused for KG2. Learners identify classrooms, office, canteen, toilets and playground, and explain why each feature is important for learning, health and safety. They begin to see the school as a well-planned environment, not just a place to be sent to.

figureLabel: Members of the school community – roles
altText: KG2 learners identifying members of the school community and discussing their different roles.
detailedDescription: The scene of headteacher, teachers, cook and caretaker is reused. KG2 learners describe what each person does, talk about how these roles help the school run smoothly, and consider how they as pupils can cooperate respectfully with each member.

figureLabel: Activities in the school – balance and participation
altText: KG2 learners looking at a picture of school activities and discussing how learning, play and eating all matter.
detailedDescription: The busy school compound picture is reused. KG2 learners talk about why a good school day includes learning, play and rest, and reflect on how they can participate well in each activity without disturbing others.

figureLabel: Texts about school – imagining better schools
altText: KG2 learners listening to a story about school life and thinking of ways to improve their own school.
detailedDescription: The school storybook scene is reused with a new focus. KG2 learners connect the pictures to their own school, suggest simple improvements such as more trees, cleaner compounds or kinder behaviour, and begin to see themselves as co-creators of a better school.

figureLabel: Safety in the school – thinking before acting
altText: KG2 learners observing risky and safe behaviours in the school compound and deciding what to do.
detailedDescription: The school safety picture is reused. KG2 learners identify both safe and unsafe behaviours, explain why some actions are dangerous, and suggest better choices, forming the habit of thinking before acting in shared spaces.

figureLabel: Living and non-living things in our environment – deeper observation
altText: KG2 learners on a nature walk observing living and non-living things and explaining why they belong to each group.
detailedDescription: The same nature walk scene is reused. KG2 learners look more closely at plants, animals and objects, describe how living things grow and change, and think about how people should care for living things and use non-living things wisely.

figureLabel: Living vs non-living – characteristics
altText: KG2 learners sorting pictures of living and non-living things and explaining the reasons for their choices.
detailedDescription: The same sorting chart used in KG1 is revisited in KG2. Learners place pictures of animals, plants and objects into ‘living’ and ‘non-living’ columns, but now they must explain using simple characteristics like grows, breathes, needs food or does not change on its own, building early logical reasoning.

figureLabel: Reading about living and non-living things
altText: KG2 learners listening to a story about living and non-living things and linking ideas in the text to real objects.
detailedDescription: The big-book scene on living and non-living things is reused. KG2 learners read and discuss why the items in the story are living or non-living, link them to objects around their school and home, and begin to use words like grow, move, and change to justify their thinking.

figureLabel: Parts of a plant – observation and description
altText: KG2 learners observing a real plant and describing the roles of roots, stem, leaves, flowers and fruits.
detailedDescription: The potted plant and chart are reused for KG2. Learners not only name each plant part but also describe what it does, such as roots taking water, leaves making food and fruits feeding people. They practise speaking in full sentences and connect science ideas to farming and food.

figureLabel: Uses of plants – thinking beyond food
altText: KG2 learners discussing pictures of food, medicine, shade and decoration that come from plants.
detailedDescription: The plant-uses picture cards are reused. KG2 learners group plant uses into food, medicine, shade, building and decoration, and talk about why caring for plants protects our food, health and homes, building gratitude and stewardship thinking.

figureLabel: Texts about plants – growth stories
altText: KG2 learners listening to a story about how a plant grows from seed to fruit and talking about each stage.
detailedDescription: The plant storybook scene is reused. KG2 learners recall and describe the stages of plant growth shown in the pictures, relate them to gardens and farms they know, and begin to sequence events using simple time words like first, next and then.

figureLabel: Caring for plants – planning actions
altText: KG2 learners looking at a picture of children watering and weeding plants and planning how to care for plants at school and home.
detailedDescription: The school garden care scene is reused. KG2 learners discuss why watering, weeding and protecting plants are important, and they make simple plans for when and how they will help care for plants at school or at home, nurturing responsibility and initiative.

figureLabel: Domestic and wild animals – comparing habitats
altText: KG2 learners sorting domestic and wild animals and discussing where each animal lives and why.
detailedDescription: The domestic and wild animal chart is reused. KG2 learners talk about where each animal lives, why some stay near people and others in the wild, and what responsibilities people have to care for domestic animals and to protect wild animals and their habitats.

figureLabel: Animal sounds and movements – patterns
altText: KG2 learners imitating animal movements and sounds and talking about how different animals move and live.
detailedDescription: The playful animal movement circle is reused. KG2 learners act out and describe how different animals move and sound, and then discuss why some animals hop, crawl or fly, connecting movement to where animals live and how they survive.

figureLabel: Texts about animals – connecting knowledge
altText: KG2 learners listening to a story about animals and connecting story facts to real animals they know.
detailedDescription: The animal storybook scene is reused. KG2 learners listen for facts about how animals eat, move and live, and then share what they know from their homes and community, practising how to connect information from texts with real experience.

figureLabel: Showing kindness to animals – responsibilities
altText: KG2 learners observing children caring for animals and discussing their responsibilities toward animals.
detailedDescription: The kindness-to-animals scene is reused for KG2. Learners identify kind and unkind actions towards animals, explain why kindness matters, and think of ways to care for animals at home and in their community, linking compassion to leadership and responsibility.

figureLabel: Sources of water – comparing and classifying
altText: KG2 learners observing different water sources such as a borehole, river, rainwater tank and pipe in a Ghanaian community.
detailedDescription: The KG1 picture of water sources is reused. In KG2, learners name each water source, talk about which ones are clean or dirty, and discuss which sources are safer for drinking and which are better only for washing or watering plants. They begin to classify water sources by safety and use.

figureLabel: Uses of water – needs and wants
altText: KG2 learners discussing pictures of people using water for drinking, cooking, washing, farming and play.
detailedDescription: The KG1 scene of water uses is reused. KG2 learners group different uses of water into ‘needs’ such as drinking, cooking, washing and farming, and ‘wants’ such as playing with water. They talk about why needs must come first when water is scarce, building early priority and resource-management thinking.

figureLabel: Texts about water – linking to real life
altText: KG2 learners listening to a story about water and connecting it to how they use water at home and school.
detailedDescription: The big-book water scene is reused. KG2 learners identify how characters in the story use water, compare that with how they use water in their homes, and talk about what happens when water is wasted or dirty. They learn to read not just for fun, but to improve daily choices.

figureLabel: Caring for water – preventing waste and contamination
altText: KG2 learners observing how to use and store water safely, such as closing taps and covering containers.
detailedDescription: The KG1 water-care picture is reused. KG2 learners notice children closing taps, covering buckets and avoiding pouring dirty water into clean water sources. They suggest their own ideas for saving water and keeping it clean, practising problem-solving and shared responsibility.

figureLabel: Presence of air – invisible but powerful
altText: KG2 learners exploring the presence of air with balloons, pinwheels and a simple fan in a Ghanaian classroom.
detailedDescription: The KG1 air experiments scene is reused. KG2 learners observe how air fills balloons, turns pinwheels and pushes a small kite or cloth. They describe what they see and explain that even though air cannot be seen, it has power to move and fill things, planting early scientific reasoning.

figureLabel: Uses of air – everyday examples
altText: KG2 learners exploring everyday uses of air such as breathing, cooling with a fan, drying clothes, and flying a kite.
detailedDescription: The KG1 uses-of-air picture is reused. KG2 learners look at breathing, fans, drying clothes and kites, and explain how air helps each activity. They begin to see that air supports life, comfort and work, not just play, building gratitude and awareness.

figureLabel: Texts about air – reading to understand
altText: KG2 learners listening to a big-book read-aloud about air and using pictures and words to understand its uses.
detailedDescription: The air big-book scene is reused. KG2 learners connect pictures of balloons, wind, trees and fans to the printed words air, wind and breathe. They talk about what they learn from the story and how it explains things they see around them, practising how to learn from texts.

figureLabel: Keeping our air clean – shared responsibility
altText: KG2 learners practising ways to keep the air clean around their school, such as avoiding smoke, covering refuse bins and watering trees.
detailedDescription: The KG1 clean-air scene is reused. KG2 learners identify actions that make air dirty, such as burning rubbish near classrooms, and actions that protect air, such as covering bins and planting trees. They suggest what they and adults should do differently, developing leadership and environmental conscience.

figureLabel: Creation as gifts to enjoy and protect
altText: KG2 learners looking at pictures of nature and talking about creation as gifts to enjoy and protect.
detailedDescription: The KG1 creation picture is reused. In KG2, learners name different things in creation, talk about how these gifts help people live, and discuss simple ways they can protect land, water, plants and animals as part of thanking God or the Creator.

figureLabel: God or Creator provides through people and nature
altText: KG2 learners discussing how food, water, family and work are ways God or the Creator provides.
detailedDescription: The KG1 scene of children receiving food and care is reused. KG2 learners list different ways they receive help—through family, farmers, teachers and nature—and see these as channels of provision. They begin to connect belief in God with gratitude, hard work and care for others, not just asking for things.

figureLabel: Reading texts about creation
altText: KG2 learners listening to a story about creation and connecting it to real land, water, plants and animals.
detailedDescription: The KG1 creation storybook scene is reused. KG2 learners listen and then point to real examples of land, water, plants and animals around them. They talk about which parts of the story are like life in Ghana and which are different, practising thoughtful, not superstitious, belief.

figureLabel: Appreciation to God – words and actions
altText: KG2 learners thanking God or the Creator through songs, prayers and responsible actions.
detailedDescription: The KG1 appreciation scene is reused. KG2 learners discuss that real appreciation is shown not only by singing and praying, but also by caring for the environment, helping others and using things wisely, connecting spirituality directly to daily behaviour.

figureLabel: Good values – naming and recognising
altText: KG2 learners looking at scenes of honesty, kindness and respect and naming the values shown.
detailedDescription: The KG1 good-values picture is reused. KG2 learners identify values such as honesty, kindness, respect and hard work in the scenes, and tell short examples from their own lives when they or others showed these values.

figureLabel: Practising values – choosing what to do
altText: KG2 learners discussing what they would do in different situations that require honesty and kindness.
detailedDescription: The KG1 practising-values scene is reused. KG2 learners look at small situations in the picture, such as dropping money or seeing a friend in trouble, and decide what they would do. They talk about how values guide choices, training an inner compass rather than fear of punishment.

figureLabel: Texts about values – learning from stories
altText: KG2 learners listening to a story about honesty, kindness or respect and linking it to their own lives.
detailedDescription: The KG1 values-story scene is reused. KG2 learners identify the main value in the story, describe how the character changed, and talk about how they can live that value at home, in school and in the community.
